finding: Failed terminal persistence can still produce a successful terminal stream event
evidence: Reproduced first: the stream said Completed while the store held Working. processor/reconcile.rs reads the store back after an ambiguous write; the terminal gate carries a Verdict; HandlerLimits::terminal_confirmation (default Required) ends the stream UNAVAILABLE when the store does not confirm. Real-model end to end (Qwen3-1.7B, llama.cpp 4fffab6, real webhook socket, store rejecting only Completed): stream [Working] then UNAVAILABLE, GetTask Working, no webhook carried Completed; BestEffort restores the old stream/store disagreement.

finding: Outbox recovery can deliver an artifact the state machine rejected
evidence: Reproduced first: a rejected append whose reservation release failed was armed by recovery once a later event moved the stored position. A processor now keeps a reservation it could not settle and stores no position past it (Invariant I); a failed write is read back before it is assumed failed.

finding: Reservation expiring during a still-running write can lose a committed event's delivery
note: Fixed for a live writer (hold renewed while the fold runs). A writer whose process dies mid-write is settled from the task store after the hold, as designed; a longer hold cannot prove an outstanding database operation will never commit.
evidence: PushOutbox::extend_hold (new, default reports unsupported; memory, SQLite and PostgreSQL implement it) lets the processor renew the hold while its fold runs (heartbeat). Not closed: a writer whose process dies mid-write is still settled from the task store after the hold, which is the designed recovery; a longer hold alone cannot prove an outstanding database operation will never commit (the reviewer's point).
tests: processor_reserve_tests/heartbeat.rs; outbox contract tests for extend_hold

finding: In-flight purge can delete historical audit records after a legal hold succeeds
note: Single-store atomic hold check and the chain lock. Residual: erase_subject against a hold placed on another replica (S8).
evidence: Reproduced first on memory and SQLite, same log and two logs: records 1 to 3 deleted after a completed hold. Deletion is now hold-checked atomically per store (delete_through_unless_held; advisory lock on PostgreSQL) and purge takes the chain lock.

finding: PostgreSQL audit append holds a transaction while sealing queries the same pool
evidence: Reproduced first: a pool of 2 timed out. Sealing now reads nothing inside append_next: subject keys and the empty-chain anchor are read before the transaction.

finding: Cold/expired JWKS fetch failures are serialised but not shared or backed off
evidence: Reproduced first: 100 requests made 100 fetches against a down endpoint. A failure is shared with the waiters, cooled down, and the waiters are bounded within the fetch deadline.

finding: Authentication and bearer tenant resolution parse headers differently
note: Proven for REST and JSON-RPC; the gRPC and WebSocket clients are not separately tested.
evidence: Reproduced first: 'BEARER tok' authenticated and its token landed in another tenant. One parser (extract_bearer) serves authentication and tenant resolution.

finding: Builder-created REST transports keep a trailing slash (double-slash route)
evidence: Reproduced first: the server answered 404 for //message:send. One canonical_base_url serves every way a RestTransport is made; 12 builds assert the request line the server received.

finding: Canonical REST tenant paths fail for route-head tenant names
note: Proven for the message, task, subscribe and card routes; push-config routes are not covered by the shape predicate's tests.
evidence: Reproduced first: tenant 'tasks' answered 404. The server routes against full templates (is_route shape predicate), not first segments.

finding: GetExtendedAgentCard discards the request tenant and skips tenant admission
evidence: Reproduced first: the provider received no tenant and strict resolution was bypassed. The tenant flows through admission and the provider on every binding (JSON-RPC, REST, gRPC, SLIMRPC).

finding: with_protocol_binding can undo version filtering
evidence: Reproduced first: an explicit JSON-RPC override selected the 0.3 /legacy interface while sending v1 requests. Both paths and build_grpc use selection::compatible_for.

finding: Required audit gates admission, not durable completion
note: Fixed in process: a refused record is kept and written, calls carry an id, a crash's unended starts are reconciled, and a tool call can be recorded before it runs. Not done: the spool is memory, no result record after a tool ran, off-machine checkpoint retention is the deployment's.
evidence: Reproduced first: [call.started, call.started] after a store outage; through a real server pending_outcomes()==0 with the records gone. A required log now spools a refused record and writes it when the store answers (bounded, counted: outcomes_lost), calls carry a server-made call id, unresolved_calls/reconcile_unresolved close starts a crash left unended with call.unresolved, and AuditedPolicy writes tool.action before a call runs and refuses a call it cannot record. NOT done: the spool is memory (a process that dies with records in it loses them; reconciliation covers calls, not task.event); a result record after a tool ran; off-machine retention of signed checkpoints (the deployment's).
tests: audit/tests/outcome_durability.rs (9); audit/tests/outcome_reconcile.rs (5); tool_loop/run_tests/audited.rs (6); tests/audit_outcome_durability.rs (real server); 21 hand mutants

finding: Approval separation trades off caller isolation
note: Opt-in (with_review_grants). How an approver learns a task is waiting is the application's; there is no list-waiting-approvals method.
evidence: ApprovalGate::with_review_grants(): a named approver sending x-a2a-review-for reaches the requester's partition for GetTask (only while the task waits for a decision) and for SendMessage/SendStreamingMessage (only an approval decision). Other methods are refused with the header; a quorum above 1 is satisfiable under isolation; the approval audit record carries reviewFor. NOT done: a list-waiting-approvals method.

finding: Raw caller-visible tool-trace artifact
note: Opt-in (TraceContent::Receipt, ToolLoop::strict). The default is unchanged and documented.
evidence: Default unchanged (documented). Receipt traces hold tool, call id and outcome, never arguments or results; checked live with Qwen3-1.7B (no canary bytes in the trace).

finding: Tool policy/tenant/approval context not integrated into the built-in loop
evidence: ToolPolicy asked before every call (native, recovered, repeated) with tenant, principal and task from the authenticated request; ArgumentCheck validates arguments against the tool's schema subset before the policy; AuditedPolicy records before it allows. Live: asked to transfer 500 against a cap of 100, the first call was refused, the model retried with 100, the policy refused, the tool ran 0 times. The remaining half, an approval bound to the call's digest, is S7 (f757caa3), on the step journal of S1.
tests: tool_loop/run_tests/strict.rs; tool_loop/schema_tests.rs (17); run_tests/schema.rs (6); tests/tool_loop_strict_live.rs; run_tests/journal_approval.rs, journal_binding.rs

finding: recover_text_calls defaults on
note: Opt-in (TextCallRecovery::Off or ReadOnly, ToolLoop::strict). The default is unchanged and documented.
evidence: Default unchanged (documented). Live: a requested JSON example stayed the answer under strict; the default loop ran the same text as an action three times, to the turn bound.

finding: Production profile does not force named principals, strict tenant resolution, intentional sharing or finite budgets
note: New profile. The authorization assertion is the deployment's; retention and erasure schedules and per-replica limits are not enforced by it.
evidence: Profile::MultiTenant applies caller isolation and strict tenant resolution and refuses build() without an authenticator, an asserted-authorized tenant resolver (with_authorized_tenant_resolver), tenant-partitioned stores, a tenant-aware store when sharing is chosen, and a concurrency limit for every tenant. The authorization assertion is the deployment's; retention/erasure and per-replica limits are not enforced.

finding: Durable step journal (resume points, pinned versions, pending approvals, action receipts)
note: A run begun again under the same key resumes, with pins, receipts, fencing and fail-closed writes, on memory, SQLite and PostgreSQL. Not done: expiry of a journal row whose run never ends, anything that begins an orphaned task again, compensation, and any two-replica test.
evidence: Control first: with no journal the same death repeats the tool (without_a_journal_the_same_death_repeats_the_call). ToolLoop::with_journal(Arc<dyn StepJournal>) writes a checkpoint (conversation, trace, calls answered, a receipt per call) after each model reply, before each call and after each; a run begun again under the same key resumes and asks the model only for what comes next. Pins: model name, digests of the preamble, tool set and modes, with_pin labels; a resume under other pins is PinMismatch. A receipt is Started before a call runs; on resume it is re-run only when with_idempotency_secret was set, else Indeterminate. A write that cannot be made stops the run before the call; a write is accepted only as the stored revision's successor. Real model (Qwen3-1.7B, llama.cpp 4fffab6): a run killed inside a call over a SQLite file resumed, the model was asked once and the tool's second call carried the first's idempotency key. NOT done: external effects still need the backend's idempotency (a repeat is rare and visible, not impossible); a journal row is removed only when its run ends, so an abandoned run keeps its row (no expiry); nothing here begins an orphaned task again (a search of the server for such a mechanism found none); compensation; fencing was tested against one store in one process, not by two replicas; PostgreSQL ran the contract test only.
tests: run_tests/journal.rs (8), journal_writes.rs (2), journal/tests.rs (5, the store contract; the PostgreSQL one needs A2A_TEST_POSTGRES_URL and includes a race of two writers for one revision), journal_approval.rs (7), journal_binding.rs (3); tests/tool_loop_approval_journal.rs (3, real handler); tests/tool_loop_journal_live.rs (3, real model, ignored); 26 hand mutants, all killed

finding: Skill content pinning (manifests over bodies and resources, deployment pins, hashes in audit evidence, revocation)
evidence: Not started. Resource files are read live from the canonical directory.

finding: Fleet-wide inference quota and cost reservation with a declared overshoot bound
evidence: Not started. The inference limiter is process-local and usage is accounting after the response.

finding: Independent visibility of telemetry export failure; collector-outage and cardinality qualification
evidence: Not examined: exporter accounting exists (otel/telemetry/counting.rs); the reviewer's point is an observer that works when the exporter does not, and measured overhead under failure.

finding: Measure docs/readiness-bar.md rows R1-R7, C1-C5, F2-F5 and publish failure and recovery evidence
note: R1 to R4 and C1 to C5 measured over HTTP JSON-RPC under L1, L3 and L4; R5, R6, R7, F1 to F5, L2 and L5 are not, and nothing is measured on two replicas or PostgreSQL.
evidence: tests/readiness_bar/ (an --ignored harness) printed every row MET in three 30 s release runs at ba335f90 (0 errors in about 400,000 requests per run; p99 1.08 to 1.16 ms against a 25 ms bar; 56 to 58 bytes per request against 1,024; fds, tokio tasks, queues and non-terminal tasks back to baseline; R4 refused 12 of 16 with a retry signal and none timed out). Recorded in docs/readiness-bar.md with host, profile, command and spread. Built with LTO off, which is not the published profile.

finding: Release evidence manifest tying the source tree to tests, waivers, supported profiles and measured limits
note: scripts/release_evidence.py generates and verifies a manifest by hand; it is not a gate in release.yml, runs no test suite and signs nothing.
evidence: generate --commit REV [--run-gates] records the commit and tree, crate versions, MSRV and toolchain, the SHA-256 of each claim-bearing input read from the commit's tree, every advisory waiver with its reason, the deployment profiles and Cargo features, the register's counts, the measured limits (a machine-readable block in docs/readiness-bar.md, each number checked against the prose table), the unreleased breaking changes and each static gate's exit status (not_run unless --run-gates). verify re-reads the inputs and fails on any mismatch, and with --head unless the manifest is for HEAD. --self-test passes 15 checks; generate then verify --head exits 0; a manifest with one input hash changed exits 1. NOT done: wiring into release.yml (it needs the gate inventory and reachability checks to learn it first); a signature; test results (CI's run of the commit holds them).

finding: Approval bound to immutable tool name, arguments, requester and scope in the built-in loop
note: For the built-in loop (ToolLoopExecutor and ToolLoop::with_journal). An executor that does its own approval through ctx.approval() binds to whatever it binds.
evidence: PolicyDecision::RequireApproval parks the run with call_digest(tool, arguments, tenant, requester, task), a SHA-256 over canonical JSON; the request id is the journal key. A decision for that digest releases that call and no other: the loop re-checks the digest, tenant and task itself, and asks the policy again (a Deny on resume still denies). A second call of the same turn that needs approval parks on its own digest. Through the real handler with the approval gate and review grants: approval runs the call once with the arguments in the journal; a decision for another action or from another caller releases nothing; a refusal completes the task and the call never runs. Real model: the model chose transfer_money {account 4417, amount 500}, the task parked with that call's digest, approval ran the tool once with those arguments, a refusal ran it 0 times.
tests: run_tests/journal_approval.rs (7); journal_binding.rs (3); tests/tool_loop_approval_journal.rs (3); tests/tool_loop_journal_live.rs (2 of 3); 26 hand mutants of the journal and approval code, all killed

finding: erase_subject against a legal hold, across replicas (A1 residual)
evidence: The per-store atomic hold check covers purge; erase_subject's interaction with a hold placed on another replica is not made atomic.

finding: main unprotected; protect-main ruleset disabled
note: A repository setting; cannot be changed from a session.
evidence: A repository setting, not code: enable required status checks, a review policy and protection of workflow files on main. Not changed from this session.

finding: A client that disconnects during a send can leave its new task Submitted for ever (found by S5's churn profile)
note: Two windows after the row is saved, both fixed. The harness read after the bar defines C4 (after L3, for 120 s) to find it.
evidence: Reproduced first: 30,000 loopback connections, half dropped before the response, left one task Submitted for the whole 120 s read in 3 of 6 runs. (1) CommitGuard learned a row existed only when the save returned; (2) the send awaited applied_mark between its commit and the task that stores the executor's events. After both fixes 0 of 13 runs left a task.
tests: handler/messaging/dropped_send_tests.rs (4: a gate at the await, a store that writes the row and never answers, a continuation that must not be rolled back, a blocking send dropped after its commit); 3 hand mutants
